blocks.text: Dohra:
Then did Captain David Murray remark, Must the author get this also recorded: The way the descendents of Mehraj and Phool1 , Extended their hold in the Malwa's forests. (1)
lines: Then did Captain David Murray remark,
Must the author get this also recorded: The way the descendents of Mehraj and Phool1 ,
Extended their hold in the Malwa's forests.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
The way the author had heard about them, From his ancient and talented peers, In the same vein did he narrate to Captain Murray, In the same manner would he get it recorded. (2)
lines: The way the author had heard about them,
From his ancient and talented peers,
In the same vein did he narrate to Captain Murray,
In the same manner would he get it recorded.

blocks.text: Dear devout readers listen to the same account, Must they record it correctly wherever he faltered. It was forested area full of innocent people, It was adjacent to the fifty two villages of Hisar Bawani. (3)
lines: Dear devout readers listen to the same account,
Must they record it correctly wherever he faltered.
It was forested area full of innocent people,
It was adjacent to the fifty two villages of Hisar Bawani.

blocks.text: As Delhi was under the occupation of Toor Rajputs, The Hisar Bawani was under Chauhan Rajput's control. The Jat subjects who lived in these forested areas, To innumerable sub castes did these Jats belong. (4)
lines: As Delhi was under the occupation of Toor Rajputs,
The Hisar Bawani was under Chauhan Rajput's control.
The Jat subjects who lived in these forested areas,
To innumerable sub castes did these Jats belong.

blocks.text: Majority of these Jats belonged to the Sidhu caste, Noble deeds must have their ancestors done. As very few odd Sidhu Jats had come here, Large chunks of land had they occupied. (5)
lines: Majority of these Jats belonged to the Sidhu caste,
Noble deeds must have their ancestors done.
As very few odd Sidhu Jats had come here,
Large chunks of land had they occupied.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Those who had occupied this land quite early, Ownership rights of land had they procured. As Mehraj (Sidhu) Jats kept wandering as nomads, Hardly could they make both their ends meet. (6)
lines: Those who had occupied this land quite early,
Ownership rights of land had they procured.
As Mehraj (Sidhu) Jats kept wandering as nomads,
Hardly could they make both their ends meet.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Chauhan Rajputs seized Delhi from the Toors, As Rai Pithora2 had played foul with them. Thereafter, he got twenty five lakh Rajputs eliminated, Who, being defenceless, was eliminated by Mohd. Ghori3 . (7)
lines: The Chauhan Rajputs seized Delhi from the Toors,
As Rai Pithora2 had played foul with them.
Thereafter, he got twenty five lakh Rajputs eliminated,
Who, being defenceless, was eliminated by Mohd.
Ghori3 .

blocks.text: As Mohammad Ghori was ousted by the (Lodhi) Pathans, Guru Nanak brought the Mughals to oust the Pathans. Let the author narrate the account of the Mughal Period, And the good times arrived for the Mehraj Sidhu Jats. (8)
lines: As Mohammad Ghori was ousted by the (Lodhi) Pathans,
Guru Nanak brought the Mughals to oust the Pathans.
Let the author narrate the account of the Mughal Period,
And the good times arrived for the Mehraj Sidhu Jats.

blocks.text: First of all let the author narrate about the Bhai4 dynasty, That would gradually lead us to Mehraj Sidhus. The first was a Bhai Behlo who became a devout Sikh, To the (fifth) Sikh Guru did go to render a service. (9)
lines: First of all let the author narrate about the Bhai4 dynasty,
That would gradually lead us to Mehraj Sidhus.
The first was a Bhai Behlo who became a devout Sikh,
To the (fifth) Sikh Guru did go to render a service.

blocks.text: An indigenous brick kiln had the Guru activated, With bricks did the Guru wish to construct a shrine at Taran Taaran. As the flames leapt out of this brick kiln, Bhai Behlo brought a bundle of garbage to douse this fire. (10)
lines: An indigenous brick kiln had the Guru activated,
With bricks did the Guru wish to construct a shrine at Taran Taaran.
As the flames leapt out of this brick kiln,
Bhai Behlo brought a bundle of garbage to douse this fire.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The moment Bhai Behlo5 got buried under the bundle, Instantly did Guru Arjan Dev ji arrived there. Praising the services of a devout Gursikh unto the Guru, Immediately did the Guru pull him out. (11)
lines: The moment Bhai Behlo5 got buried under the bundle,
Instantly did Guru Arjan Dev ji arrived there.
Praising the services of a devout Gursikh unto the Guru,
Immediately did the Guru pull him out.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the revered Guru felt pleased with Bhai Behlo's services, The congregation of forested areas was put under his charge. This information did Bhai Bhagtoo also receive, As he went to pay his obeisance to the revered Guru. (12)
lines: As the revered Guru felt pleased with Bhai Behlo's services,
The congregation of forested areas was put under his charge.
This information did Bhai Bhagtoo also receive,
As he went to pay his obeisance to the revered Guru.

blocks.text: In the same manner as Bhai Bhagtoo touched the Guru's feet, The Guru appointed him incharge of another forest area. As two more Sikhs Haria and Balo6 accompanied Bhai Bhagtu, The whole forest area got blessed by the Guru. (13)
lines: In the same manner as Bhai Bhagtoo touched the Guru's feet,
The Guru appointed him incharge of another forest area.
As two more Sikhs Haria and Balo6 accompanied Bhai Bhagtu,
The whole forest area got blessed by the Guru.

blocks.text: Now would the author narrate the account of Mehraj dynasty, Narrate he would as he had heard from his old elders. As Mehraj ancestors were the last to approach the Guru, No land was left that could be allotted to them. (14)
lines: Now would the author narrate the account of Mehraj dynasty,
Narrate he would as he had heard from his old elders.
As Mehraj ancestors were the last to approach the Guru,
No land was left that could be allotted to them.

blocks.text: Thus, in whomsoever's house they went to seek shelter, The owner would treat them as his subjects. As they could not occupy any land on their own, Listen further how these Mehraj ancestors progressed. (15)
lines: Thus, in whomsoever's house they went to seek shelter,
The owner would treat them as his subjects.
As they could not occupy any land on their own,
Listen further how these Mehraj ancestors progressed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Mehraj elders had many scheduled caste men with them, They employed them for diverse menial jobs. For this reason they became the butt of ridicule of those, Who had been earlier inhabitants of these forest areas. (16)
lines: As Mehraj elders had many scheduled caste men with them,
They employed them for diverse menial jobs.
For this reason they became the butt of ridicule of those,
Who had been earlier inhabitants of these forest areas.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Mehraj elders had dealings with these lower castes, They remained at loggerheads with the natives. As the natives considered Mehraj elders mighty and powerful, They were apprehensive that the latter might occupy their land. (17)
lines: As the Mehraj elders had dealings with these lower castes,
They remained at loggerheads with the natives.
As the natives considered Mehraj elders mighty and powerful,
They were apprehensive that the latter might occupy their land.

blocks.text: So the natives never-allowed the latter to stay at one place, They would charge rentals if allowed them to stay. So as these Mehraj elders kept moving like nomads, They had to pass through such a heavy ordeal. (18)
lines: So the natives never-allowed the latter to stay at one place,
They would charge rentals if allowed them to stay.
So as these Mehraj elders kept moving like nomads,
They had to pass through such a heavy ordeal.

blocks.text: Thus would they be turned out from the area, With the joint efforts of the natives and their custodians. Upon this did the Mehraj elders made a resolve, Must they also occupy an area for their subsistence. (19)
lines: Thus would they be turned out from the area,
With the joint efforts of the natives and their custodians.
Upon this did the Mehraj elders made a resolve,
Must they also occupy an area for their subsistence.

blocks.text: (But) how could they occupy land in an alien land, Unless someone mighty and powerful assisted them. As good fortune smiled on these wandering elders, (Fifth) Guru's protection did they proceed to seek. (20)
lines: (But) how could they occupy land in an alien land,
Unless someone mighty and powerful assisted them.
As good fortune smiled on these wandering elders,
(Fifth) Guru's protection did they proceed to seek.

blocks.text: Sortha:
So approaching Bhai Bhagtoo, With folded hands did they bow down. Narrating their tale of woe, For Guru's blessings should he intercede. (21)
lines: So approaching Bhai Bhagtoo,
With folded hands did they bow down.
Narrating their tale of woe,
For Guru's blessings should he intercede.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Vaisakhi festival was approaching near, Mohan (from Mehraj 's family) did Bhai Bhagtoo take along. After introducing the former to the whole congregation, With folded hands did they stand before the Guru. (22)
lines: As the Vaisakhi festival was approaching near,
Mohan (from Mehraj 's family) did Bhai Bhagtoo take along.
After introducing the former to the whole congregation,
With folded hands did they stand before the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
The moment the revered Guru looked at them smilingly, Instantly did they feel blessed indeed. Mehraj 's grandson Mohan had come along with Bhagtoo, Who had brought his own son Kala with him. (23)
lines: The moment the revered Guru looked at them smilingly,
Instantly did they feel blessed indeed.
Mehraj 's grandson Mohan had come along with Bhagtoo,
Who had brought his own son Kala with him.

blocks.text: Then to the revered Guru did Mohan offer Kala's services, All the collections did they also pile up before the Guru. Kala offered his services to the Guru's community kitchen, Thereafter, all the disputes of the devotees did the Guru settle. (24)
lines: Then to the revered Guru did Mohan offer Kala's services,
All the collections did they also pile up before the Guru.
Kala offered his services to the Guru's community kitchen,
Thereafter, all the disputes of the devotees did the Guru settle.

blocks.text: Thereafter Baba Mohan laid bare his heart before the Guru, For a piece of land for his clan's settlement did he ask. Smilingly did the revered Guru tell Baba Mohan: He (the Guru) wished to empower Mohan to give lands to others. (25)
lines: Thereafter Baba Mohan laid bare his heart before the Guru,
For a piece of land for his clan's settlement did he ask.
Smilingly did the revered Guru tell Baba Mohan: He (the Guru) wished to empower Mohan to give lands to others.

blocks.text: From him (Baba Mohan) would the people beg for land, For the time being should he go back with Bhai Bhagtu. Soon would he (the Guru) pay a visit to the forested area, All his (Baba Mohan's) cherished desires would the Guru fulfil then. (26)
lines: From him (Baba Mohan) would the people beg for land,
For the time being should he go back with Bhai Bhagtu.
Soon would he (the Guru) pay a visit to the forested area,
All his (Baba Mohan's) cherished desires would the Guru fulfil then.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thereupon, Baba Mohan begged the revered Guru, Where would his clan seek shelter till then? Thereupon, did the revered Guru assured him, The Divine Creator would protect him where he stayed. (27)
lines: Thereupon,
Baba Mohan begged the revered Guru,
Where would his clan seek shelter till then?
Thereupon, did the revered Guru assured him,
The Divine Creator would protect him where he stayed.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, Bhai Bhagtu offered them shelter for stay, Thus did this nomadic clan find a home for themselves. As the original land owners objected to their stay, They did not stop objecting even after Bhai Bhagtu's pleas. (28)
lines: Thereafter,
Bhai Bhagtu offered them shelter for stay,
Thus did this nomadic clan find a home for themselves.
As the original land owners objected to their stay,
They did not stop objecting even after Bhai Bhagtu's pleas.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the revered Guru brought out a miracle, Through an emperor's act did the Guru caused this marvel. That emperor's account would the author now narrate, The way he had heard that tale from his learned peers. (29)
lines: Thereafter, the revered Guru brought out a miracle,
Through an emperor's act did the Guru caused this marvel.
That emperor's account would the author now narrate,
The way he had heard that tale from his learned peers.

blocks.text: There used to be one emperor Chattarsal in the South, Day and night did he keep himself in an inebriated state. Many a hardship did his subjects keep passing through, Being an alcoholic how could he address people's grievances? (30)
lines: There used to be one emperor Chattarsal in the South,
Day and night did he keep himself in an inebriated state.
Many a hardship did his subjects keep passing through,
Being an alcoholic how could he address people's grievances?

blocks.text: Dohra:

His enemies who surrounded him from neighbouring states, A lot of his territory did they occupy (forcibly). His ministers and court officials tried their best, Many a counsel did they offer to the king in vain. (31)
lines: His enemies who surrounded him from neighbouring states,
A lot of his territory did they occupy (forcibly).
His ministers and court officials tried their best,
Many a counsel did they offer to the king in vain.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Utmost did his mother, brother and his wife try, But little did he pay any heed to their advice. As he remained in an inebriated state day and night, All affairs of state remained in a state of chaos. (32)
lines: Utmost did his mother, brother and his wife try,
But little did he pay any heed to their advice.
As he remained in an inebriated state day and night,
All affairs of state remained in a state of chaos.

blocks.text: As these news reached the sovereign at (Delhi), He bestowed Chattarsal's state's custody to his younger brother. Chattarsal was ordered to be put behind the bars, Two bottles of liquor were sanctioned for his daily consumption. (33)
lines: As these news reached the sovereign at (Delhi),
He bestowed Chattarsal's state's custody to his younger brother.
Chattarsal was ordered to be put behind the bars,
Two bottles of liquor were sanctioned for his daily consumption.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The ministers of the state following this royal decree, They fixed an auspicious occasion for the new king's anointment. A few hours after the break of dawn on that day, They would anoint his younger brother with the royal title. (34)
lines: The ministers of the state following this royal decree,
They fixed an auspicious occasion for the new king's anointment.
A few hours after the break of dawn on that day,
They would anoint his younger brother with the royal title.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Though Chattarsal's wife heard this new order, Nothing could she do despite her desperate pleadings. As Chattarsal craved for more alcohol, he woke up his wife, For a goblet of alcohol did he press his wife. (35)
lines: Though Chattarsal's wife heard this new order,
Nothing could she do despite her desperate pleadings.
As Chattarsal craved for more alcohol, he woke up his wife,
For a goblet of alcohol did he press his wife.

blocks.text: His younger brother would offer him that, his queen said, Soon after the day break would his brother arrive. As he again asked for alcohol in harsh words, In still harsher words did his queen reprimand. (36)
lines: His younger brother would offer him that, his queen said,
Soon after the day break would his brother arrive.
As he again asked for alcohol in harsh words,
In still harsher words did his queen reprimand.

blocks.text: His younger brother would definitely come with a royal decree, The royal decree for his kingship would he handover. With fetters around his feet would his brother offer a goblet, Let a few hours pass after day break on that day. (37)
lines: His younger brother would definitely come with a royal decree,
The royal decree for his kingship would he handover.
With fetters around his feet would his brother offer a goblet,
Let a few hours pass after day break on that day.

blocks.text: Hearing this did Chattarsal come to his senses, After that did he ask for a reprieve from his wife. Must the king make haste to escape from there, Before Jahangir must he beg for restoration of his rule. (38)
lines: Hearing this did Chattarsal come to his senses,
After that did he ask for a reprieve from his wife.
Must the king make haste to escape from there,
Before Jahangir must he beg for restoration of his rule.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As he heard this news (from his wife), Instantly did he mount his royal steed. Arriving at the royal court posthaste, His predicament did he narrate to the king. (39)
lines: As he heard this news (from his wife),
Instantly did he mount his royal steed.
Arriving at the royal court posthaste,
His predicament did he narrate to the king.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon Jahangir7 refused his petition, Now would he not get any reprieve from the court. Many a time had the emperor reprimanded him in writing, Never did he give up drinking at the king's bidding. (40)
lines: Thereupon Jahangir7 refused his petition,
Now would he not get any reprieve from the court.
Many a time had the emperor reprimanded him in writing,
Never did he give up drinking at the king's bidding.

blocks.text: Hearing this, did Chattarsal beg the king with folded hands, Some alternative means of livelihood must the king grant. Thereupon, the emperor put forth another proposal, A decree for Malwa forests could he get if he ransacked those. (41)
lines: Hearing this, did Chattarsal beg the king with folded hands,
Some alternative means of livelihood must the king grant.
Thereupon, the emperor put forth another proposal,
A decree for Malwa forests could he get if he ransacked those.

blocks.text: Arriving at Bathinda did he put up a camp, As nothing could he get for food in the forests. He summoned the official custodians of that area, As he found the whole territory a barren land. (42)
lines: Arriving at Bathinda did he put up a camp,
As nothing could he get for food in the forests.
He summoned the official custodians of that area,
As he found the whole territory a barren land.

blocks.text: When he enquired about possible means of livelihood, The official custodians suggested means of loot and plunder. As Chattarsal asked them to provide guidance to him, He offered to destroy those who defied the legal custodians. (43)
lines: When he enquired about possible means of livelihood,
The official custodians suggested means of loot and plunder.
As Chattarsal asked them to provide guidance to him,
He offered to destroy those who defied the legal custodians.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Mehraj 's clan had been a thorn in their flesh, The custodians put forth their name for ransacking. As the Mehraj clan settlers received this news, Highly concerned did they feel for their safety. (44)
lines: As Mehraj 's clan had been a thorn in their flesh,
The custodians put forth their name for ransacking.
As the Mehraj clan settlers received this news,
Highly concerned did they feel for their safety.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hearing this Mehraj 's clan approached Bhai Bhagtu, The entire situation did they narrate to him. As none else could protect them, said Bhai Bhagtu, Must they pray with folded hands to the revered Guru. (45)
lines: Hearing this Mehraj 's clan approached Bhai Bhagtu,
The entire situation did they narrate to him.
As none else could protect them, said Bhai Bhagtu,
Must they pray with folded hands to the revered Guru.

blocks.text: With devotion did they pray to the Divine Guru, Might the Guru protect them from that scourage. Such a divine dispensation came to happen there, That another caravan of displaced people arrived there. (46)
lines: With devotion did they pray to the Divine Guru,
Might the Guru protect them from that scourage.
Such a divine dispensation came to happen there,
That another caravan of displaced people arrived there.

blocks.text: With these new arrivals did the Mehraj clan confabulate, By deserting the place would they never survive. As they were still confabulating to fight together, They came to be invaded by Chattarsal's troops. (47)
lines: With these new arrivals did the Mehraj clan confabulate,
By deserting the place would they never survive.
As they were still confabulating to fight together,
They came to be invaded by Chattarsal's troops.

blocks.text: As his troops ransacked the Jat settlers, They sent messengers to their Mehraj clan allies. With a dash did the Mehraj members attack, They invaded Chattarsal's troops with a beat of drums. (48)
lines: As his troops ransacked the Jat settlers,
They sent messengers to their Mehraj clan allies.
With a dash did the Mehraj members attack,
They invaded Chattarsal's troops with a beat of drums.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As they robbed the Chattarsal's troops to their fill, They brought the bundles full of robbed goods. The king Chattarwal was abandoned by his troops, His troops went their own ways from the field. (49)
lines: As they robbed the Chattarsal's troops to their fill,
They brought the bundles full of robbed goods.
The king Chattarwal was abandoned by his troops,
His troops went their own ways from the field.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
As the king remained alone on the field, No longer could he fight with Mehraj 's force. As the king was killed there by the Mehrajians, The Divine Guru solved all their problems. (50)
lines: As the king remained alone on the field,
No longer could he fight with Mehraj 's force.
As the king was killed there by the Mehrajians,
The Divine Guru solved all their problems.

blocks.text: As they went in hot pursuit of the royal troops, All those troops were robbed by the Mehraj clan. As such a dispensation did the Guru bring about, How could the troops fight without a king? (51)
lines: As they went in hot pursuit of the royal troops,
All those troops were robbed by the Mehraj clan.
As such a dispensation did the Guru bring about,
How could the troops fight without a king?
